Char: Study name: Effect of vitamin B12 supplementation on anthropometric indices in children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) aged 1 month to 60 month in a nutritional rehabilitation center - a randomised control trial
Char: Participants:
180 children (target enrolment) , 1-60 months of age with severe acute malnutrition. Children will be allocated to 1 of 2 groups.

Inclusion criteria: children with severe acute malnutrition, defined as mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) < 11.5 cm and/or weight for height/length less than 3 standard deviations and/or bilateral pitting edema

Exclusion criteria: children with unstable vitals, non-nutritional anemia, chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, gastrointestinal disorders, heart disease or infantile tremor syndrome
Char: Interventions:
Intervention: vitamin B12 500 µg/day plus multiple micronutrients (vitamin A 50,000-200,000 units according to age for one day, folic acid 1 mg/day for 14 days, zinc 2 mg/kg/day for 14 days, iron 3 mg/kg/day for 1 month, magnesium 0.4 mmol/kg/day for 14 days, potassium 3 meq/kg/day for 14 days, copper 0.3 mg/kg/day for 14 days)

Control: multiple micronutrients alone

Duration: 12 months
Char: Outcomes: Change in weight and height at 12 months. Change in haemoglobin, mean copuscular volume, anaemia prevalence and type of anaemia at 12 months
